instructions: Find the colour shared by two cubes. Put both cubes of that colour directly on {mat}, and put the remaining cube in {container}.
Group the repeated-colour pair on {mat}; store the cube whose colour occurs only once inside {container}.
Two cubes have the same colour and one is different. Place the matching pair directly on {mat} and the odd-coloured cube in {container}.
Sort by whether a cube has a colour mate: cubes with a mate go on {mat}, and the cube without a mate goes in {container}.
First identify the two same-coloured cubes and move both onto {mat}. Then put the differently coloured cube into {container}.
The final arrangement should have the repeated-colour pair resting directly on {mat} and the unique-coloured cube inside {container}.
notes: Assigns destinations by colour frequency within the scene rather than by a named colour or matching destination colour.
